newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends lower on soy tumble, new low in Dec.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends lower on soy tumble, new low in Dec.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on a collapse in the soy complex and on improved crop conditions with a new contract low posted in new crop December, traders said.
The new low for December is $2.32-1/4, below the previous low of $2.33-3/4 set Monday.
USDA Monday said the U.S. corn crop as of Sunday was 74 percent good to excellent, improved from the 67 percent in that category the previous week.
Also current U.S. Midwest weather and weather forecasts remain nearly perfect for crop development, sources noted.
The National Weather Service six- to 10-day outlook Monday was for below normal temperatures and above normal precipitation in the Midwest from July 6 to July 10.
Corn closed 1-1/2 to 6-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with July down 4-3/4 at $2.43-1/4. December was down 5-1/2 cents at $2.32-3/4.
The lack of large scale export business recently, coupled with spillover pressure from Friday's USDA Hogs and Pigs report also contributed to the declines in corn, traders said.
USDA on Friday revealed the U.S. hog herd was not expanding to the extent earlier expected.
USDA reported hogs kept for breeding were up one percent from a year earlier. The figure was well under pre-report estimates which ranged from three to six percent gains in breeding hog numbers.
Griffin Trading sold six million bushels of December, Smith Barney sold three million December and Term Commodities sold 3.5 million bushels of December, traders said.
Cargill Inc bought 5.5 million bushels of September, ADM Investor Services bought 3.5 million bushels of December and Refco Inc bought and sold two million bushels of December, traders said.
In spread trading, LIT America did three million bushels of July/December at 10 cents, premium July, Griffin Trading did two million December/July at 10 cents, premium July, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 72,000 contracts, below the 103,131 traded Monday.

In corn options, Continental Grain sold 800 December $2.80 calls at 3-1/4 to 3-1/8 cents, LIT America sold 500 December $2.00 calls at 34 cents and ABN Amro-The Chicago Corp sold 300 December $2.70 puts at 38-1/4 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 23,000 contracts, below the 25,435 traded Monday.
